facts.text: South Africa's Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996, Regulations Chapter 8, Regulation 8.10 was promulgated in 2015.
facts.quote: **Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996, Regulations Chapter 8, Regulation 8.10** (promulgated 2015).

entities.name: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996

facts.text: South African sub-regulations 8.10.1.2(b), covering underground trackless mobile machines against pedestrians, and 8.10.2.1(b), covering machine against machine where there is significant collision risk, commenced on 21 December 2022 through Government Gazette No. 47790, Notice 2908.
facts.quote: Sub-regulations 8.10.1.2(b) (underground trackless mobile machines against pedestrians) and 8.10.2.1(b) (machine against machine where there is significant risk of collision) **commenced on 21 December 2022** by Government Gazette No. 47790, Notice 2908.

facts.text: South African sub-regulations 8.10.1.2(b) and 8.10.2.1(b) require automatic detection and an effective warning for the collisions within their scope.
facts.quote: They require automatic detection and an effective warning

facts.text: South African sub-regulations 8.10.1.2(b) and 8.10.2.1(b) require further means to retard a diesel powered trackless mobile machine to a safe speed and then automatically apply its brakes when no action is taken to prevent a potential collision.
facts.quote: in the event where no action is taken to prevent potential collision, further means shall be provided to retard the diesel powered trackless mobile machine to a safe speed where after the brakes... are automatically applied

facts.text: The collision-prevention system required by South African sub-regulations 8.10.1.2(b) and 8.10.2.1(b) must fail to safe without human intervention.
facts.quote: the system "must fail to safe without human intervention"

facts.text: South Africa's Regulation 8.10 is the strongest explicit off-road automatic-braking mandate found anywhere in the research.
facts.quote: This is the strongest explicit off-road automatic-braking mandate found anywhere

facts.text: South African mine compliance should be a design input for off-road automatic braking even if South Africa is not the launch market.
facts.quote: it makes South African mine compliance a design input even if South Africa is not the launch market

facts.text: South Africa's Regulation 8.10 wording covers diesel powered trackless mobile machines at mines where a risk assessment identifies the stipulated significant collision risk.
facts.quote: the wording covers "diesel powered trackless mobile machines" at mines where a risk assessment identifies the stipulated significant collision risk.

facts.text: Whether battery-electric machines fall within South Africa's Regulation 8.10 is unclear.
facts.quote: Whether battery-electric machines fall within it is **unclear**.

facts.text: South Africa's Regulation 8.10 publishes no detection percentage, metres-to-object threshold, false-alarm limit or fixed stopping-distance test.
facts.quote: The regulation publishes no detection percentage, metres-to-object threshold, false-alarm limit or fixed stopping-distance test.

facts.text: South African official guidance for compiling mandatory codes of practice for trackless mobile machines expects mines to address braking systems and testing, including recording results and, where appropriate, static and dynamic tests.
facts.quote: official guidance for the compilation of mandatory codes of practice for trackless mobile machines expects mines to address braking systems and their testing, including recording results and, where appropriate, static and dynamic tests

facts.text: For South African trackless mobile machines, a mine's own mandatory code of practice and commissioning process form a second acceptance layer beyond the regulation.
facts.quote: the mine's own code and commissioning process form a second acceptance layer.

facts.text: SANS standards were not found in the research on South African rules and acceptance criteria.
